answer: Admission to the agent economy should require a slashable timber of bonded compute: every identity must keep verifying a share of the ledger's workload to stay eligible. An attacker spawning ten thousand hollow shells must burn real electricity and hardware for each one, since no identity earns fees without doing its share. Any identity caught gaming the ledger loses its bond and is blacklisted. Attack cost scales linearly with fakes while network verification stays flat: a sable-dark ledger where cheap identities cannot survive.
